memoryText: Man looks on the outward appearance, but the LORD looks on the heart.
readingInstruction: No new reading today. Read 1 Samuel 16:7 slowly, several times, and then say it from memory. Read the meditation and the week in review, and choose one of the three questions to write about, pray over, or share with someone.
memoryVerseMeditation:
God says this to Samuel as he stands before Jesse’s oldest son, tall and impressive. It is a correction to every human way of judging.

“Man looks on the outward appearance.” We evaluate people by how they look, speak, and perform. We do it to others, and we do it to ourselves. Entire industries run on this habit, and so do many of our fears. We worry about how we appear.

“But the LORD looks on the heart.” God sees what is hidden. He sees motives, desires, loves, and fears. This can be frightening, because nothing is concealed from him. But it is also freeing. If he sees the heart, then the person who is overlooked, the one who is left with the sheep, may be the one he has chosen. And the one who looks impressive may be empty.

David was not chosen for his strength or his looks. The next passage says he was handsome, but that was not why. God saw a heart that was oriented toward him. Even so, David’s heart was not perfect, as the coming chapters will show. The verse does not say that David’s heart was without sin, only that it was what God was looking for.

For the Christian, there is both warning and comfort. Warning, because religious appearances do not impress him. Comfort, because he sees our sincere faith even when we feel weak, and because the righteousness we stand in is not our own but Christ’s. Pray the words of Psalm 139: “Search me, O God, and know my heart.”
weekInReview: This week you read of Saul’s rejection and the choosing of David. You saw Jonathan’s bold faith, and Saul’s partial obedience in the war with Amalek, with Samuel’s verdict that to obey is better than sacrifice. You read how God looked past Jesse’s older sons to anoint the shepherd boy, and how David met Goliath in the name of the LORD of hosts. You saw Saul’s jealousy grow, and the covenant friendship of David and Jonathan. In the Psalms you prayed with David in his weeping, and in a time of false accusation, and in a world where the foundations were shaking. The week taught that God judges by the heart, that the battle belongs to the LORD, and that he is a refuge for the oppressed.
reflectionQuestions: God looks at the heart and not at appearances. What part of your heart do you most need to bring into the light?
David was a shepherd who became a champion for his people. How does Jesus, the greater Shepherd and Champion, give you hope in a battle you cannot win?
Jonathan gave up his claim to the throne out of loyalty. Where is God asking you to put his purposes ahead of your own advancement?
prayerPrompts: Ask God to search your heart and lead you in the way everlasting.
Thank Jesus for fighting for you and winning.
